keyword: how fast does the artemis rocket go

verifications.claim: The Artemis Space Launch System (SLS) rocket reaches speeds of approximately 17,000 to 18,000 mph to achieve orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'When the rocket's main engines shut down eight minutes after liftoff, the rocket will be moving at some 18,000 mph.' R5: 'the rocket goes soaring off into space at approximately 17,000 mph.'
verifications.reasoning: References directly support the speed range for achieving orbit after core stage burnout.

verifications.claim: The Artemis Space Launch System (SLS) rocket reaches speeds of about Mach 22 to achieve orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'It's the equivalent to 22 times the speed of sound.'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match for Mach 22 equivalence at orbital speed.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule reaches speeds over 25,000 mph upon reentry.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R2: 'peak reentry speed will be slightly over 25,000 mph'. R3: 're-entered Earth's atmosphere at a maximum velocity of about 24,664 miles per hour'
verifications.reasoning: R2 supports expected speed over 25,000 mph; R3 reports actual speed under 25,000 mph, creating contradiction.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule reaches speeds of approx. 40,000 km/h upon reentry.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Both references support approximately 40,000 km/h (40,200 and 39,693 are both approx. 40,000).

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule sets records for the fastest speed for a crewed spacecraft.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Greatest reentry speed (and fastest humans in history)'. R3: 'maximum velocity... is comparable to those reached during lunar-return missions of the Apollo program.'
verifications.reasoning: R2 claims it sets record; R3 states comparable to Apollo (not explicitly record-breaking), indicating potential contradiction.

verifications.claim: The Artemis Space Launch System (SLS) rocket puts the Orion capsule into orbit traveling at roughly 17,500 mph.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: 17,500 mph is roughly the average of directly stated orbital insertion speeds.

verifications.claim: The upper stage accelerates the Orion capsule toward the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'The rocket's upper stage will increase the velocity to 22,600 mph... to... send the Orion capsule to the moon.'
verifications.reasoning: Direct support, though technically ESM performs TLI post-separation; reference attributes to upper stage.

verifications.claim: The upper stage reaches speeds sometimes exceeding 22,600 mph during translunar injection.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R4: 'upper stage will increase the velocity to 22,600 mph — 110 football fields per second — to break out of Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Reference states exactly 22,600 mph for translunar injection, not exceeding; 'sometimes' makes it broader.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is expected to hit over 25,000 mph when returning from the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'NASA estimates that the crew's peak reentry speed will be slightly over 25,000 mph'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match for expected reentry speed.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is expected to hit over 40,000 km/h when returning from the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Direct match for expected reentry speed in km/h.

verifications.claim: The reentry speed for the Artemis II crew is expected to be faster than that of any other humans in history.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'the Artemis II crew will also reenter... at slightly higher speeds than any other astronauts in history... fastest humans in history'
verifications.reasoning: Direct support for expected record-breaking reentry speed.

verifications.claim: The slow-moving transport vehicle that takes the Artemis Space Launch System (SLS) rocket to the launchpad moves at less than 1 mph.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The crawler... will reach a top speed of 0.8 mph'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match for crawler-transporter speed under 1 mph.
